songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Viola Lee Blues jam and soaring Morning Dew
ai_show_review.blurb: Features a blistering Viola Lee Blues and an inspired Morning Dew with Jerry's soaring lead guitar. Alligator and the extended psychedelic stretch keep the set high‑octane, though the audience tape suffers frequent drop‑outs.
ai_show_review.review: The September 15, 1967 Hollywood Bowl show captures the Dead at a wild, exploratory peak. The band launches straight into a ferocious Viola Lee Blues that stretches into uncharted territory before pulling back into tight, melodic moments like Cold Rain And Snow and Beat It On Down The Line. Jerry's lead work soars on Morning Dew, riding Phil's thumping fretless bass, while Pigpen’s organ‑harmonica duels add an extra layer of grit. Alligator rolls into a psychedelic cascade that segues seamlessly into Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) and a noisy Feedback finale, showcasing the group's willingness to push boundaries. Though only an audience recording exists—marred by hiss, muffled mids, and occasional drop‑outs—the tape conveys the raw excitement of the night and remains the sole document of this historic set.

best_recording.reason: Only existing source; despite drop‑outs it captures the raw, high‑energy performance and period ambience.
